papers.title: Structure-guided computational design of DNA tweezers for predicted recognition of the primary glioblastoma biomarkers S100A4 and midkine.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is among the most aggressive malignant brain tumors and is characterized by severe infiltration into surrounding brain tissue, rendering early detection exceedingly difficult with current diagnostic imaging methods. Chosen biomarkers S100A4, with a role in cell motility and tumor metastasis, and midkine (MDK), connected to tumor microenvironment remodeling and expansion, are both linked to GBM's infiltrative proliferation. This study investigates a computational framework for the structure-guided design of DNA tweezer nanostructures, evaluated for predicted intera
papers.summary: This study presents a computational framework for designing DNA tweezer nanostructures that are predicted to recognize two key glioblastoma biomarkers, S100A4 and midkine. The work aims to improve early detection of this aggressive brain tumor by targeting proteins linked to its invasive growth.

papers.title: First Report of (E)-1-Phenyl-3,7-dimethyl-2-octen-1-ol and N-propyl-4-methoxycinnamamide from Aegle marmelos unripe fruit: Isolation, characterization and mechanistic evaluation of proton pump inhibitory and antioxidant activities.
papers.abstract: Aegle marmelos (L.) Corr. (Rutaceae) is a medicinally important tree widely used across South Asia for the treatment of gastrointestinal disorders including peptic ulcers, diarrhea, and dysentery. Beyond its antiulcer applications, the plant has been reported to possess antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and cytoprotective activities. However, the specific bioactive compounds and mechanisms underlying proton pump inhibition remain insufficiently characterized at the molecular level.To isolate and characterize bioactive constituents from the unripe fruit of A. marmelos responsible f
papers.summary: This study identifies two new compounds from unripe Aegle marmelos fruit that inhibit proton pumps and have antioxidant activity, providing a molecular basis for the plant's traditional use against peptic ulcers. The findings suggest these compounds could be developed as natural alternatives for managing gastric acid-related disorders.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics analysis suggests a potential mechanism of DEHP-induced monocyte infiltration in MASH via the FOS-CCL3/4 axis.
papers.abstract: Di-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) is a widespread environmental obesogen; however, its immune-proinflammatory mechanisms in the progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) remain incompletely elucidated. This study aims to comprehensively characterize the core targets and molecular mechanisms by which DEHP disrupts the hepatic microenvironment and drives disease progression through multi-omics integration and experimental analysis.
papers.summary: This study investigates how the environmental chemical DEHP contributes to liver inflammation in MASH by integrating multi-omics data. The authors identify a FOS-CCL3/4 signaling axis that promotes monocyte infiltration into the liver, providing a mechanistic link between DEHP exposure and immune-driven disease progression.

papers.title: BBP acts as an exogenous modulator of MMP9 to rewire vascular immunity and promote atherosclerosis.
papers.abstract: Environmental exposure to endocrine-disrupting chemicals has been increasingly implicated in cardiovascular disease, yet the causal molecular mechanisms linking such exposures to atherosclerosis remain incompletely defined. Benzyl butyl phthalate (BBP), a widely used plasticizer, has been associated with vascular dysfunction, but its mechanistic contribution to atherogenesis is unclear. Here, we employed an integrative systems biology framework combining network toxicology, transcriptomic profiling, protein-protein interaction network analysis, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations
papers.summary: This study uses a systems biology approach to show that the plasticizer BBP promotes atherosclerosis by modulating MMP9, rewiring vascular immunity. The findings provide a mechanistic link between environmental chemical exposure and cardiovascular disease.

papers.title: Comprehensive analysis of the molecular dynamics of bisphenol compounds and prediction of their effects on prostate cancer progression.
papers.abstract: Bisphenols are a class of widely occurring environmental endocrine disruptors, but a comprehensive understanding of their systemic effects on prostate cancer progression under conditions of low-concentration exposure remains lacking. This study established a comprehensive research framework integrating bioinformatics analysis, functional experiments, and structural biology analysis to systematically evaluate the cancer-promoting effects of eight bisphenol compounds, namely, BPA, BPAF, BPB, BPC, BPE, BPF, BPS, and BPZ, in prostate cancer. Enrichment analysis revealed that, across cancer types,
papers.summary: This study integrates bioinformatics, functional experiments, and structural biology to evaluate how eight bisphenol compounds (e.g., BPA, BPS) promote prostate cancer progression at low concentrations. The findings reveal shared cancer-promoting molecular pathways across these endocrine disruptors, providing a systematic understanding of their environmental health risks.

papers.title: Structural and functional effects of carbonylation and phosphorylation on the Zu5-ANK domain: A molecular dynamics and docking study.
papers.abstract: 4-HNE carbonylation and phosphorylation in the Zu5-ANK domain have been observed in human erythrocytes with sickle cell trait and G6PD deficiency. However, the atomic-level effects of phosphorylation and multiple carbonylations by 4-HNE on the Zu5-ANK domain are not yet fully understood. The present work provides further insight into understanding the changes caused by polymodifications in Zu5-ANK due to oxidative stress and phosphorylation. Here, we present a molecular dynamics simulation-based study of the polycarbonylated, phosphorylated, and phosphocarbonylated Zu5-ANK domain. Our results
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how carbonylation and phosphorylation modifications alter the structure and function of the Zu5-ANK domain, which is relevant to sickle cell trait and G6PD deficiency. The findings provide atomic-level insights into how these post-translational modifications, induced by oxidative stress, affect protein behavior.

papers.title: Antidiabetic potential of a novel hydroxyphenyl-bi-benzopyran-hexol compound from Cassia fistula as an α-amylase inhibitor: Integrated in silico screening and in vitro validation using a nonlinear regression model.
papers.abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a critically important metabolic disease, causing persistent hyperglycemia. Blood glucose levels can be effectively maintained by inhibiting the activity of α-amylase. α-amylase inhibitors manage postprandial hyperglycemia by delaying carbohydrate digestion.
papers.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
papers.summary: This study identifies a novel compound from Cassia fistula that inhibits α-amylase, an enzyme involved in carbohydrate digestion, suggesting potential for managing postprandial blood sugar in diabetes. The authors used computational screening and lab experiments with a nonlinear regression model to validate the compound's activity.

papers.title: Integrated computational and experimental evidence of biochemical and physiological perturbations induced by environmentally relevant thallium exposure in Daphnia magna.
papers.abstract: Thallium (Tl), a highly toxic heavy metal, poses a serious threat to freshwater ecosystems. This study investigated the chronic toxicity of Tl(I) in Daphnia magna using an integrated approach combining network toxicology, molecular docking, and biochemical assays. Network analysis identified 23 candidate enzyme targets, with significant enrichment in pathways related to glutathione metabolism, suggesting a potential involvement of antioxidant regulation in Tl(I)-induced toxicity. Molecular docking indicated energetically favorable spatial associations between Tl(I) and several enzymes, suggest
papers.summary: This study combines computational predictions with lab experiments to show that environmentally relevant levels of thallium disrupt antioxidant pathways and key enzymes in Daphnia magna, a freshwater crustacean. The findings highlight glutathione metabolism as a central target, providing a mechanistic understanding of thallium's chronic toxicity in aquatic ecosystems.

papers.title: Water-soluble β-strand peptidomimetics.
papers.abstract: Mediation of protein-protein interactions with molecules that bind strongly and selectively to one of the partners at the protein interface is a promising therapeutic strategy for myriad diseases. One such approach is the rational design of non-peptidic scaffolds that reproduce the display of amino acid side chains from one face of a secondary structural element. We have previously disclosed proof-of principle syntheses of β-strand mimetics composed of alternating (hetero)aromatic and cyclic urea units, conformationally preorganised through dipolar repulsion in organic solvents, that are in go
papers.summary: This paper describes the design and synthesis of water-soluble β-strand peptidomimetics that can mimic protein secondary structures for therapeutic applications. The authors developed conformationally preorganized scaffolds composed of alternating aromatic and cyclic urea units that maintain their structure in aqueous environments.

papers.title: Quantitative correlation of spectroscopic signatures with ligand-protein interactions in anti-cancer drug Afinitor: an integrated experimental-computational study.
papers.abstract: A detailed molecular-level understanding of anticancer drugs is essential for improving therapeutic efficacy and guiding rational drug design. Everolimus (Afinitor), a clinically important inhibitor of the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway, is widely used in cancer therapy; however, a quantitatively grounded relationship between its spectroscopic characteristics and ligand-protein interactions remains insufficiently explored. In this study, an integrated experimental-computational approach was employed, combining FT-IR spectroscopy, UV-Vis spectroscopy, and molecular docking simulat
papers.summary: This study combines experimental spectroscopy (FT-IR, UV-Vis) with molecular docking to quantitatively link the spectroscopic signatures of the anti-cancer drug Everolimus (Afinitor) to its interactions with the mTOR protein. The integrated approach provides a molecular-level understanding of the drug's binding, which could aid in rational drug design.

papers.title: AlphaFold-driven structural proteomics reveals extensive cellulosome machinery in human ruminococcal symbionts.
papers.abstract: Cellulosomes are large, surface-displayed enzyme complexes that enable anaerobic bacteria to degrade recalcitrant plant polysaccharides, yet cellulosome-expressing bacteria are thought to be rare in the human gut. Here, we show that extensive sequence divergence obscures the detection of many ruminococcal cellulosomes by conventional sequence homology-based methods. Using proteome-scale AlphaFold2 structural predictions, we uncovered a substantially expanded set of putative cellulosome-producing Ruminococcus species, including six previously unrecognized human symbionts. Structure-based cluste
papers.summary: This study uses AlphaFold2 structural predictions to discover that many more Ruminococcus species in the human gut produce cellulosomes than previously thought, overcoming limitations of traditional sequence-based methods. The findings reveal six previously unrecognized human symbionts with cellulosome machinery, expanding our understanding of plant polysaccharide degradation in the gut microbiome.

papers.title: Rhubarb extract attenuates periodontitis by modulating an MMP3-associated inflammatory-ferroptotic axis: Integrated multi-omics analysis and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease characterized by dysregulated host immunity, oxidative injury, connective tissue breakdown, and alveolar bone loss. Rhubarb (Rhei Radix et Rhizoma) has anti-inflammatory and redox-modulating properties, but its therapeutic mechanism in periodontitis remains unclear.
papers.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
papers.summary: This study shows that rhubarb extract can reduce periodontitis severity by targeting an MMP3-associated inflammatory-ferroptotic pathway, as revealed by integrated multi-omics analysis and validated experimentally. The findings suggest a new therapeutic mechanism for rhubarb in treating periodontal disease.

papers.title: A Bayesian Approach to Interpret Time-Resolved Experiments Using Molecular Simulations.
papers.abstract: Time-resolved experiments can provide unique insights into dynamic processes such as protein folding, ligand binding, and many other molecular processes. These experiments are, however, difficult to interpret at the molecular level because they generally report on signals that are averaged over multiple configurational states and because they often report on processes that are well beyond what can be studied using most simulation methods. Here, we describe an approach to use molecular simulations to model and interpret time-resolved experiments. The method, which we term trBME (time-resolved B
papers.summary: This paper introduces trBME, a Bayesian method that uses molecular simulations to model and interpret time-resolved experiments, which are often difficult to analyze due to signal averaging over multiple molecular states. The approach helps bridge the gap between experimental data and molecular-level understanding of dynamic processes like protein folding and ligand binding.

papers.title: System-Size Effects on the Molecular Dynamics Simulation of an All-Aromatic Liquid Crystal.
papers.abstract: Atomistic molecular dynamics simulations are presented for a prototypical all-aromatic calamitic liquid crystal that has recently emerged as a benchmark system for testing theories of nematic order. By performing simulations with progressively larger systems, up to an unprecedented total of 12,600 molecules, we investigate the impact of system size on the structural and dynamic properties of the material in the nematic and smectic A mesophases. Our results demonstrate that using a number of molecules on the order of 104 not only improves statistical sampling, thereby reducing uncertainty in al
papers.summary: This study uses large-scale molecular dynamics simulations (up to 12,600 molecules) to show that using ~10^4 molecules significantly improves statistical sampling and reduces uncertainty in simulating an all-aromatic liquid crystal. The findings provide practical guidance for choosing system sizes in future simulations of liquid crystals.

papers.title: Docking of virtual libraries identifies small-molecule agonists of neurotensin receptors with analgesic activity.
papers.abstract: Peptide-activated G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) play crucial roles in numerous diseases, but remain difficult therapeutic targets due to the challenges in developing small-molecule drugs. Here, we explore structure-based strategies to identify small-molecule agonists of neurotensin (NTS) receptors, which hold promise for developing non-opioid analgesics. Chemical libraries of drug-like molecules are first designed based on a receptor-peptide complex, and then 14.5 million compounds are computationally docked to the orthosteric binding site of the NTS1 receptor. A set of 39 top-ranked com
papers.summary: This study used computational docking of 14.5 million virtual compounds to identify small-molecule agonists of neurotensin receptors, which are promising targets for non-opioid pain relief. The approach successfully found drug-like molecules that activate the receptor, offering a new strategy for developing analgesics without the side effects of opioids.

papers.title: Ensemble Docking and Molecular Dynamics Indicate Dynamic Modulation of hnRNPA1 UP1 Interdomain Behavior by Natural Products.
papers.abstract: RNA-binding proteins exhibit substantial conformational plasticity that complicates structure-based ligand discovery and computational characterization. In this study, we applied an integrated computational approach combining high-throughput virtual screening, molecular dynamics simulations, ensemble docking, and interaction energy analysis to examine ligand binding and associated dynamic effects in the UP1 domain of hnRNPA1. Screening of 2847 phytochemicals followed by scaffold-diverse molecular dynamics evaluation identified three representative ligandsAmentoflavone, Ginkgetin, and Withanol
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods to investigate how natural products bind to the UP1 domain of hnRNPA1, an RNA-binding protein. The authors identified three phytochemicals that modulate the protein's dynamic behavior, which could inform future drug discovery efforts targeting such conformationally flexible proteins.

papers.title: AlphaDTA: integrating AlphaFold3 embeddings and 3D complex structures for drug-target binding affinity prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target binding affinity plays an important role in structure-based drug discovery, yet existing approaches are constrained by their reliance on scarce experimentally determined protein-ligand complex structures. In this context, recent advances in biomolecular structure prediction models, such as AlphaFold3, have emerged as a promising approach to alleviate the scarcity of experimentally determined protein-ligand complex structures. In this study, we introduce AlphaDTA, a framework that integrates AlphaFold3-predicted structures and embeddings for drug-target bindin
papers.summary: AlphaDTA is a new computational framework that uses AlphaFold3-predicted protein structures and embeddings to predict how strongly a drug binds to its target, overcoming the problem of limited experimental data. By integrating predicted 3D complex structures with deep learning, it improves binding affinity predictions for drug discovery.

papers.title: Structure-based functionality of a multi-domain periplasmic chitodextrinase from marine bacterium Vibrio cholerae.
papers.abstract: Periplasmic chitodextrinase (Chdx) is involved in chitin metabolism in Vibrio species. Chdxs from Vibrio cholerae (VcChdx) and Vibrio harveyi consist of six domains: an N-terminal family 5/12 carbohydrate-binding module (N-CBM), two immunoglobulin-like domains (IgL-1 and IgL-2), a GH18 catalytic domain (CatD), a chitin-binding domain (ChBD), and a C-terminal family 5/12 carbohydrate-binding module (C-CBM). We produced recombinant VcChdx, which exhibited a single band at 116 kDa on SDS-PAGE. VcChdx was successfully crystallized in ligand-free and bound state with the inhibitor allosamidin, prov
papers.summary: This study reports the structure and function of a multi-domain chitodextrinase from Vibrio cholerae, revealing how its six domains work together to break down chitin. The crystal structures of the enzyme, both alone and bound to an inhibitor, provide insights into its catalytic mechanism and substrate binding. These findings advance our understanding of chitin metabolism in marine bacteria and could inform biotechnological applications.

papers.title: Learning from trypsin(ogen) structures: conformational flexibility and functional disorder.
papers.abstract: Our understanding of trypsin, its zymogenicity and its inhibition is intimately intertwined with the history of biochemistry. Early structural studies revealed its close relationship to chymotrypsin, with its active site triad, oxyanion hole and N-terminus involved in a buried salt bridge near the active site. Its complex with basic pancreatic trypsin inhibitor provided a model for how peptide substrates bind to and are cleaved by the proteinase. Analysis of crystals of trypsinogen by Wolfram Bode and Robert Huber revealed that a large region of the zymogen is disordered prior to proteolytic a
papers.summary: This review discusses how structural studies of trypsin and its inactive precursor trypsinogen have revealed key insights into conformational flexibility and functional disorder in proteins. The authors highlight how early work on trypsinogen showed that large regions can be disordered before activation, and how the trypsin-inhibitor complex became a model for understanding substrate binding and cleavage.

papers.title: Enhancing virtual screening of cystathionine β-synthase inhibitors: benchmarking target-specific machine-learning scoring functions against state-of-the-art AI docking and co-folding approaches.
papers.abstract: Cystathionine β-synthase (CBS) has emerged as an important therapeutic target implicated in cancer and Down syndrome, yet the discovery of selective CBS inhibitors remains challenging due to limited structural diversity of known ligands and the scarcity of target-focused virtual screening (VS) benchmarks. In this study, we present the first comprehensive evaluation of CBS-specific artificial intelligence (AI) models for structure-based VS, supported by a carefully curated and up-to-date data set of experimentally validated CBS inhibitors, true inactives and decoys. Using this data set, we deve
papers.summary: This study presents the first comprehensive evaluation of AI-based virtual screening methods for identifying inhibitors of cystathionine β-synthase (CBS), a therapeutic target in cancer and Down syndrome. The authors curated a benchmark dataset of validated CBS inhibitors and decoys, then compared target-specific machine learning models against state-of-the-art AI docking and co-folding approaches. Their findings provide guidance for improving the discovery of selective CBS inhibitors.

papers.title: AI-assisted fragment-based drug discovery of SARS-CoV-2 macrodomain binders validated by NMR and X-ray crystallography.
papers.abstract: Fragment-based drug discovery (FBDD) is an effective approach for exploring chemical space using small, low-affinity fragments as starting points to facilitate development of lead compounds. Strategies to improve fragment potency include fragment merging and linking to generate higher-affinity inhibitors. Recently, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have accelerated this process through structure-based optimization and generative compound design. Here, we present an AI-assisted FBDD workflow applied to the SARS-CoV-2 macrodomain (Mac1), a conserved viral protein involved in
papers.summary: This study presents an AI-assisted fragment-based drug discovery workflow targeting the SARS-CoV-2 macrodomain, a conserved viral protein. The approach uses machine learning for structure-based optimization and generative design to improve fragment potency, with hits validated by NMR and X-ray crystallography.

papers.title: 4MRNA: a new approach for nucleic acid molecular replacement using models with diverse parameter patterns.
papers.abstract: Structural analysis of nucleic acids lags behind that of proteins, partly because most fundamental structural analysis techniques have been primarily developed for proteins. The molecular replacement (MR) method, commonly used for phase determination in protein crystallography, encounters unique challenges when applied to nucleic acids. Nucleic acids can have different three-dimensional structures even with the same sequence, which often renders database entries or predicted models unsuitable as search models for MR. To overcome the limitation, we developed a novel strategy termed 4MRNA, which
papers.summary: This paper introduces 4MRNA, a new computational method for molecular replacement in nucleic acid crystallography that addresses the challenge of nucleic acids adopting multiple 3D structures from the same sequence. By using models with diverse parameter patterns, 4MRNA improves the success rate of phase determination for nucleic acid structures, helping to close the gap between nucleic acid and protein structural analysis.

papers.title: Mechanistic insight into signal bias by the agonist-dependent conformational dynamics of GPR84.
papers.abstract: GPR84 is an orphan class A GPCR primarily expressed in immune cells, where it plays key roles in inflammation and metabolism. Here, we present the cryo-electron microscopy structures of the GPR84-Gi complex bound to the G protein-biased agonist DL-175, and the inactive state of GPR84 bound to the antagonist GLPG1205. Combined with signaling assays and molecular dynamics simulations, these structures elucidate the conformational landscape spanning the inactive and G protein-biased active states of GPR84, providing a mechanistic basis for biased agonism. Notably, steric interactions between DL-1
papers.summary: This study uses cryo-electron microscopy to reveal the structures of the GPR84 receptor bound to a biased agonist and an antagonist, showing how different ligands stabilize distinct conformations that lead to biased signaling. The findings provide a mechanistic understanding of how GPR84, an immune cell receptor, can selectively activate certain downstream pathways, which may inform the design of more targeted anti-inflammatory drugs.

papers.title: Cryo-EM structure of a single-chain β1-adrenoceptor - AmpC β-lactamase fusion protein.
papers.abstract: The insertion of fusion proteins has enabled the crystallization of a wide range of G-protein-coupled receptors. Here, we adapted this engineering strategy to cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM). We inserted the soluble protein AmpC β-lactamase into the third intracellular loop (ICL3) of ultra-thermostable β1-adrenoceptor (β1AR) via chimeric helix fusions. Biochemical and biophysical characterization showed that the resulting fusion protein after expression, solubilization and purification was monodisperse and able to bind the known β1AR weak partial agonist cyanopindolol, and the antagonist pr
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that inserting a soluble protein (AmpC β-lactamase) into a G-protein-coupled receptor (β1-adrenoceptor) can produce a stable fusion protein suitable for cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structural determination, extending a common crystallization strategy to cryo-EM. The fusion protein remained functional, binding known ligands, suggesting this approach could help solve structures of other membrane proteins that are challenging for cryo-EM.

papers.title: In silico design and validation of high-affinity RNA aptamers for SARS-CoV-2 comparable to neutralizing antibodies.
papers.abstract: Nucleic acid aptamers hold promise for clinical applications, yet understanding their molecular binding mechanisms to target proteins, and efficiently optimizing their binding affinities, remain challenging. Here, we present CAAMO (Computer-Aided Aptamer Modeling and Optimization), which integrates in silico aptamer design with experimental validation to accelerate the development of aptamer-based RNA therapeutics. Starting from the sequence information of a reported RNA aptamer, Ta, for the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, our CAAMO method first determines its binding mode with the spike protein's r
papers.summary: This study presents CAAMO, a computational method that integrates in silico design with experimental validation to optimize RNA aptamers targeting the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. The approach successfully generated high-affinity aptamers with binding comparable to neutralizing antibodies, demonstrating a generalizable strategy for developing RNA therapeutics.

papers.title: Structural insights into multitargeting Mycobacterium tuberculosis Pkn kinases.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis remains one of the leading major global health challenges, driven by the emergence of multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant bacterial strains. Resistant strains complicate treatment, which often requires prolonged use of toxic second- and third-line drugs. Protein phosphorylation plays critical roles in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, with serine/threonine kinases PknA, PknB, and PknG being essential for survival, virulence, and persistence. In this study, we screened an in-house kinase inhibitor library to identify compounds targeting these kinases. Four structurally div
papers.summary: This study identifies compounds that inhibit three essential serine/threonine kinases (PknA, PknB, PknG) in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, offering a potential strategy to combat drug-resistant tuberculosis. By screening a kinase inhibitor library, the authors found four structurally diverse inhibitors that target these kinases, which are critical for bacterial survival and virulence.

papers.title: Phytochemical profiling, network pharmacology, and molecular dynamics simulations of Sinularia levi metabolites as potential α-glucosidase inhibitors in metabolic syndrome.
papers.abstract: This study has investigated the phytochemical composition and therapeutic potential of the Red Sea soft coral Sinularia levi. Five compounds (1-5) comprising three glyceryl derivatives, a ceramide, and a diterpene were isolated and characterized. To elucidate their role in metabolic syndrome, an integrated network pharmacology and structure-based modeling workflow was employed. This approach identified 45 shared targets between S. levi metabolites and disease proteins, clustered into inflammatory and metabolic nodes, with α-glucosidase (GAA) emerging as a primary target. Molecular docking agai
papers.summary: This study isolated five compounds from the Red Sea soft coral *Sinularia levi* and used network pharmacology and molecular docking to identify α-glucosidase as a key target for treating metabolic syndrome. The findings suggest these marine-derived metabolites may serve as potential α-glucosidase inhibitors, offering a new avenue for drug discovery against metabolic disorders.

papers.title: ProtPen combines sequence- and structure-based approaches to facilitate protein function predictions on a proteome-wide scale.
papers.abstract: Proteins of unknown function represent a significant gap in our understanding of biological processes, encompassing large portions of the proteomes of many organisms, especially prokaryotes. Addressing this gap is critical to understanding the biology and pathogenicity of such organisms. We introduce ProtPen, an open-source pipeline that facilitates protein function prediction by combining eggNOG-mapper for sequence-based annotation with Foldseek for rapid structural similarity searches using AlphaFold-predicted protein structures. Annotation results from both tools are merged and enriched wit
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: ProtPen is a new open-source pipeline that improves protein function prediction by combining sequence-based annotation (eggNOG-mapper) with rapid structural similarity searches (Foldseek) using AlphaFold-predicted structures. This approach helps fill the gap in understanding proteins of unknown function, especially in prokaryotes, by merging and enriching annotations from both methods on a proteome-wide scale.

papers.title: Ligand-agnostic off-target site prediction for early toxicity screening by leveraging point cloud-based protein cavity analysis.
papers.abstract: Adverse drug reactions caused by molecules binding unintended targets are a major concern in drug discovery. Early identification of such interactions during drug design and development minimizes risks and enhances therapeutic efficacy. While experimental approaches are time-consuming and resource-intensive, in silico virtual screening offers a faster, cost-effective strategy to anticipate off-target effects early in drug design. Here, we present a point cloud-based virtual screening method, designed to perform off-target identification based solely on the chemical composition of the primary d
papers.summary: This paper presents a new computational method that uses point cloud-based analysis of protein cavities to predict off-target drug interactions without needing to know the ligand structure. The approach enables faster and cheaper early toxicity screening in drug discovery by identifying unintended protein targets based solely on the primary target's chemical composition.

papers.title: Graph-based drug-target interaction modeling: from representation learning to output-driven drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Graph-based deep learning has emerged as a powerful framework for modeling drug-target interactions (DTIs), enabling the integration of molecular, structural, and systems-level information within a unified representation. In this review, we survey graph-based DTI models across biomedical network-, sequence/hybrid-, and structure-based paradigms, which form a continuum from large-scale association inference to structure-resolved interaction modeling with increasing mechanistic specificity. Beyond architectural advances, we introduce an output-driven perspective in which models are evaluated acc
papers.summary: This review surveys graph-based deep learning methods for modeling drug-target interactions, covering network-based, sequence/hybrid, and structure-based approaches. It introduces an output-driven perspective for evaluating these models, highlighting their role in drug discovery.

papers.title: Recent Progress in the Development of Selective MAGL Modulators (2020-2026).
papers.abstract: Monoacylglycerol lipase (MAGL) is a key enzyme at the interface between the endocannabinoid system and lipid metabolism, playing a pivotal role in the hydrolysis of the endocannabinoid 2-arachidonoylglycerol and in the regulation of lipid mediators involved in inflammation, pain, neurodegeneration and cancer. Owing to its therapeutic relevance, MAGL has emerged as an attractive pharmacological target, stimulating extensive research efforts aimed at the development of potent and selective modulators of its activity. Advances in medicinal chemistry, together with the increasing application of in
papers.summary: This review covers recent progress (2020-2026) in developing selective modulators of monoacylglycerol lipase (MAGL), a key enzyme linking the endocannabinoid system to lipid metabolism and implicated in inflammation, pain, neurodegeneration, and cancer. It highlights advances in medicinal chemistry and the growing application of new techniques to create potent and selective MAGL-targeting compounds.

papers.title: Stimuli-Responsive Aggregation-Induced Emission Materials for Tumor Theranostics: Design Strategies and Biomedical Applications.
papers.abstract: Smart-responsive aggregation-induced emission (AIE) materials have emerged as promising bio-nanomaterials for tumor diagnosis and therapy due to their enhanced fluorescence in aggregated states, overcoming the aggregation-caused quenching of traditional fluorophores. These materials enable the construction of efficient imaging and therapeutic platforms in complex biological environments. Stimuli-responsive AIE systems can be categorized into pH-, redox-, thermo-, enzyme-responsive, and externally triggered types. Despite significant progress in AIE-based tumor imaging and therapy, critical cha
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent advances in stimuli-responsive aggregation-induced emission (AIE) materials for tumor diagnosis and therapy, which overcome traditional fluorophore limitations by enhancing fluorescence in aggregated states. The authors categorize these smart materials by response type (pH, redox, temperature, enzyme, or external triggers) and discuss their design strategies and biomedical applications, while also highlighting remaining challenges for clinical translation.

papers.title: FlowDock: A unified flow-based framework for flexible protein-ligand docking and binding affinity prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of protein-ligand complexes and binding affinity is critical for hit identification and optimization for structure-based drug design. Traditional docking simulates binding processes with searching algorithms guided by energy-scoring functions, which are quite computationally expensive and time-intensive. In contrast, deep learning approaches offer a cost-effective alternative, yet often generate conformations with limited physicochemical validity and fail to account for protein flexibility. To address these pitfalls, we propose FlowDock, a multitask framework enhanced by Ba
papers.summary: FlowDock is a new deep learning framework that simultaneously predicts protein-ligand binding poses and binding affinity, addressing limitations of traditional docking (slow) and prior AI methods (poor physical validity, no protein flexibility). By using a flow-based model, it generates physically realistic, flexible protein-ligand complexes efficiently, offering a promising tool for structure-based drug design.

papers.title: Molecular glue degraders: Rational design, specificity engineering, and advanced delivery.
papers.abstract: Molecular glue degraders (MGDs) have emerged as a transformative modality in the field of targeted protein degradation (TPD), enabling the selective elimination of disease-relevant proteins, including those traditionally considered undruggable. Unlike bifunctional proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs), MGDs operate through monovalent architectures that induce protein-protein interactions (PPIs) between E3 ligases and neosubstrates, offering advantages in chemical simplicity, cell permeability, and target scope. However, MGD discovery remains serendipitously, and a translational framework th
papers.summary: This review discusses molecular glue degraders (MGDs), a promising class of drugs that eliminate disease-causing proteins by inducing interactions between E3 ligases and target proteins, offering advantages over traditional PROTACs in simplicity and cell permeability. The authors highlight challenges in rational design and delivery while outlining strategies for engineering specificity and advancing these degraders toward clinical translation.

papers.title: In Silico Rational Design of Novel 1,3,4-Oxadiazole Thioether Derivatives for the Discovery of Xanthomonas oryzae Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: A series of newly designed 1,3,4-oxadiazole derivatives demonstrated highly effective inhibitors against Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae (Xoo) and exhibited significant antiviral and anti-biofilm properties. To further explore the structure-activity relationships of these compounds and develop novel molecules with higher activity, this study systematically analyzed the relationship between the structure and activity of a series of 1,3,4-oxadiazole compounds using computational methods including 3D-QSAR, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations. Based on a dataset containing 39 compo
papers.summary: This study used computational methods like 3D-QSAR and molecular docking to design new 1,3,4-oxadiazole thioether derivatives that effectively inhibit the bacterium Xanthomonas oryzae, which causes rice blight. The designed compounds also showed antiviral and anti-biofilm activity, offering potential new leads for crop protection.

papers.title: De Novo Synthesis in Cancer Immunotherapy: Applications and Prospects.
papers.abstract: De novo protein design enables the creation of proteins with entirely novel structures and biological functions from scratch, offering a promising new paradigm for cancer immunotherapy. Emerging methodologies are integrating principles of rational design, including specificity, modularity, and adaptability, into the development process from the outset. This innovative strategy holds the potential to advance how people understand and intervene against malignancy, through the strategic utilization of immune checkpoint regulation, cytokine engineering, cellular therapy, and signaling pathway remo
papers.summary: This review discusses how de novo protein design—creating proteins with entirely new structures and functions from scratch—can be applied to cancer immunotherapy. It highlights strategies like immune checkpoint regulation, cytokine engineering, and cellular therapy that leverage rational design principles to improve treatment specificity and adaptability.

papers.title: Integrated Phytochemical Characterisation, Pharmacological Evaluation and Computational Investigation of Acampe papillosa Stem Extract.
papers.abstract: Acampe papillosa, an orchid species traditionally utilised as an herbal medicine, has yet to be extensively researched for its potential pharmacological properties. This study examined the potential for anti-anxiety, sedative, anti-inflammatory and antipyretic effects of methanol extract of the stem of A. papillosa (APSME) through in vivo and in silico approaches. A dose of 200 and 400 mg/kg was administered to Swiss albino rodents. When examined in the elevated plus maze, APSME-treated mice spent significantly longer periods of time in the open arms of the maze at both dosages than control an
papers.summary: This study investigates the pharmacological potential of a methanol extract from the stem of the orchid Acampe papillosa, traditionally used in herbal medicine. Using in vivo experiments in mice and in silico computational analysis, the authors found that the extract exhibited anti-anxiety, sedative, anti-inflammatory, and antipyretic effects, with treated mice spending more time in the open arms of an elevated plus maze, indicating reduced anxiety.

papers.title: Multilevel in silico structural analysis of WNT proteins.
papers.abstract: WNTs are a family of signaling proteins involved in numerous biological processes, including morphogenesis, oncogenesis, cell migration and proliferation, cellular specialization, and tissue regeneration. WNT proteins are characterized by a distinctive structure comprising two domains resembling a "thumb" and an "index finger," which enables their interaction with cellular receptors. Despite the identification of 19 WNT proteins in humans, three-dimensional structural data are available for only a subset, highlighting the importance of studying WNT proteins using in silico approaches. This stu
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods to analyze the structures of WNT signaling proteins, which are important for development and cancer but have limited experimental 3D data. The authors focus on the conserved 'thumb' and 'index finger' domains that allow WNTs to bind receptors.

papers.title: BoltzOmics: Predicting genetic variant effects on drug binding with Boltz-2.
papers.abstract: A mechanistic understanding of how genetic variants alter drug-receptor binding is central to precision medicine, drug response prediction, and drug development. Yet, experimental mutation-drug profiling remains slow and expensive, while existing computational approaches often trade accuracy for scalability. We developed BoltzOmics, an interactive, open-source platform that integrates Boltz-2, a deep learning model for biomolecular structure prediction, to rapidly assess mutation effects on drug binding. Starting from amino acid sequences, the workflow queries databases for genetic variants, g
papers.summary: BoltzOmics is an open-source platform that uses the deep learning model Boltz-2 to predict how genetic variants affect drug binding to proteins, starting from amino acid sequences. It aims to provide a fast and scalable alternative to experimental mutation-drug profiling for precision medicine and drug development.

papers.title: Translating viral genetic data to PRRSV-2 cross-neutralization using machine learning.
papers.abstract: Swine herd immunization through modified live vaccination or live virus inoculation is a core strategy for controlling porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome (PRRS), one of the most economically important endemic diseases in the United States that is caused by PRRSV-2. While antigenically homologous PRRSV-2 viruses are expected to elicit better immunological cross-protection, questions remain as to how genetic similarity translates to the degree of cross-protection elicited between the immunizing strain and subsequent challenge virus. For PRRSV-2, virus neutralization (VN) assays are co
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning to predict how genetic similarity between PRRSV-2 strains translates to cross-neutralization, which is key for vaccine development. By analyzing viral genetic data, the model can estimate the degree of immunological cross-protection between immunizing and challenge viruses. This approach offers a practical tool for improving swine herd immunization strategies against this economically important disease.

papers.title: Therapeutic assessment of Nerium oleander-derived exosome-like nanoparticles against triple-negative breast cancer: a preliminary in vitro and network pharmacology approach.
papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive subtype lacking estrogen, progesterone, and HER2 receptors, which restricts targeted therapies and contributes to poor survival. Conventional chemotherapeutics such as doxorubicin and cisplatin show limited efficacy, significant toxicity, and resistance, underscoring the need for alternative strategies. Nerium oleander, a traditional medicinal plant, has demonstrated anticancer activity through leaf extracts; however, the role of exosome-like nanoparticles derived from its flowers (NELNs) remains unexplored.
papers.summary: This study explores exosome-like nanoparticles from Nerium oleander flowers as a potential treatment for triple-negative breast cancer, using lab experiments and computational network analysis. The nanoparticles showed anticancer activity in cell lines, suggesting a novel plant-based therapeutic approach for this aggressive cancer type.

papers.title: Discovery of novel peptidomimetics against HSP90-HOP interactions towards improved cancer therapeutics using machine learning strategies.
papers.abstract: The HSP90-HOP interaction orchestrates transfer of client proteins from HSP70 to HSP90, promoting their conformational maturation and stabilisation and thereby sustaining oncogenic signalling. The study explores a promising alternative for cancer chemotherapy by targeting this interface rather than the traditional ATP-binding site, which may circumvent the toxicity associated with classical HSP90 inhibitors. Despite its therapeutic relevance, the HSP90-HOP interface remains underexplored, particularly in the context of structure-guided peptidomimetic inhibitors, highlighting a critical gap in
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning to discover new peptidomimetic compounds that block the interaction between HSP90 and HOP proteins, a key step in cancer cell survival. By targeting this protein-protein interface instead of the traditional ATP-binding site, these inhibitors may offer a less toxic alternative for cancer therapy. The work addresses an underexplored area in cancer drug discovery using computational methods.

papers.title: Virtual screening of Kocuria oceani AT-1 metabolites as potential maize growth regulators under drought conditions using molecular docking and dynamics simulation.
papers.abstract: Maize is a vital cereal crop, severely affected by environmental factors and climate change. Among abiotic factors, drought stress is considered one of the most detrimental factors limiting plant growth and biomass production. However, the molecular basis of bacterial metabolite-mediated drought tolerance in cereal crops remains poorly understood. The current in silico study aimed to investigate the molecular interactions between Kocuria oceani AT-1 metabolites and the maize UGT706F8 protein, using molecular docking and dynamics simulation analyses. The molecular interactions between bacterial
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods (molecular docking and dynamics simulations) to predict how metabolites from the bacterium Kocuria oceani AT-1 might interact with a maize protein (UGT706F8) to improve drought tolerance. The work provides an in silico foundation for understanding bacterial metabolite-mediated stress responses in crops, though it remains purely computational without experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrated computational analysis identifies FABP4, PTGS2, and HPGD as Key molecular targets linking PET microplastic exposure to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects 25-38% of the global population, yet the contribution of environmental polyethylene terephthalate (PET) microplastics to its pathogenesis remains unclear. PET microplastics accumulate in the liver at approximately 4.6 particles per gram of tissue and have been implicated in metabolic disturbance, oxidative stress, and inflammation, but their molecular targets and mechanisms in MASLD are not well defined.
papers.summary: This study uses computational analysis to identify three key molecular targets—FABP4, PTGS2, and HPGD—that may link PET microplastic exposure to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). The findings suggest that PET microplastics accumulating in the liver could contribute to MASLD pathogenesis through these targets, which are involved in metabolic disturbance, oxidative stress, and inflammation.

papers.title: Orientation of Gp96 and Calreticulin T-cell epitopes in a multiepitope HPV16 E7 vaccine construct affects predicted immunostimulatory properties: An in silico and expression validation study.
papers.abstract: Heat shock proteins (HSPs) can be used as adjuvants to develop therapeutic vaccines, as they enhance the cross-presentation of related tumor antigens and stimulate T cells. In this study, the immunostimulatory properties of gp96 and calreticulin was evaluated to enhance HPV16 E7-based vaccines effectiveness. In silico evaluation was performed to select epitopes from HSPs based on high binding affinity to MHC-I/II, strong immunogenicity, and population coverage. Six novel multiepitope constructs harboring conserved epitopes of E7, gp96, and calreticulin were designed in different orientations.
papers.summary: This study computationally designed and validated multiepitope vaccine constructs against HPV16 E7 by incorporating T-cell epitopes from heat shock proteins gp96 and calreticulin as adjuvants. The orientation of these epitopes within the constructs was found to affect predicted immunostimulatory properties, with in silico and expression analyses supporting the potential of optimized designs.

papers.title: Evaluation of the cellular impact of missense variants in low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 6 (LRP6) associated with cardiovascular diseases in HeLa and HEK293T cell lines.
papers.abstract: Low-density lipoprotein (LDL) receptor-related protein 6 (LRP6) is crucial for the canonical wingless signaling pathway and the clearance of LDL from the bloodstream. Genetic variants in the LRP6 gene have been conclusively associated with cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) and metabolic syndrome. However, the structural, cellular, and functional implications of these variations have not been fully elucidated. In this study, we examined the subcellular localization, stability, and degradation of 10 LRP6 missense variants (K82N, R360H, Y418H, N433S, R473Q, S488Y, R611C, P1066T, P1206H, and I1264V)
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study characterized 10 missense variants in the LRP6 gene linked to cardiovascular disease, finding that most variants did not significantly alter protein localization or stability in HeLa and HEK293T cells. The results suggest that these variants may affect LRP6 function through more subtle mechanisms, such as altered signaling or protein interactions, rather than gross cellular mislocalization or degradation.

papers.title: Integrative analysis of FAERS, network toxicology, and Mendelian randomization identifies potential targets in paclitaxel-associated systemic sclerosis.
papers.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare and complex autoimmune disease characterized by fibrosis of the skin and internal organs as well as vascular abnormalities. Studies have suggested that paclitaxel may induce adverse reactions resembling systemic sclerosis; however, the underlying mechanisms remain not fully understood. We retrieved reports of paclitaxel-associated SSc from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS). Potential shared targets between paclitaxel and SSc were identified through network toxicology analysis. Mendelian randomization (MR) was then used to explore associations bet
papers.summary: This study investigates the link between the chemotherapy drug paclitaxel and the development of systemic sclerosis (SSc), a rare autoimmune disease. By analyzing FDA adverse event reports, network toxicology, and Mendelian randomization, the authors identify potential molecular targets that may explain how paclitaxel could trigger SSc-like adverse reactions. The findings provide new insights into drug-induced autoimmunity and highlight candidate targets for further research.

papers.title: Binding characteristics of chemosensory protein 11 from Grapholita molesta Busck (Lepidoptera: Tortricidae) to insecticides.
papers.abstract: Chemosensory proteins (CSPs) are small soluble proteins that recognize and bind to various small chemical molecules. Although numerous studies have shown that CSPs play an important role in olfactory communication among insects, recent research indicated that CSPs also contribute to insecticide resistance. The antennae-enriched GmolCSP11 from Grapholita molesta Busck exhibits high binding affinities for seven insecticide ligands, as verified by fluorescence competitive binding assays of recombinant protein. GmolCSP11 exhibited the strongest binding affinity for chlorpyrifos (Ki = 1.01 ± 0.00 μ
papers.summary: This study shows that a chemosensory protein (GmolCSP11) from the oriental fruit moth can bind strongly to several insecticides, with the highest affinity for chlorpyrifos. The findings suggest that this protein may contribute to insecticide resistance in this pest species.

papers.title: Structural Modeling of Protein-DNA Interactions Underlying Genome Copy Number Variation in Nanoviruses.
papers.abstract: Multipartite nanoviruses possess multiple segmented genomes that accumulate at unequal levels during infection, giving rise to dynamic genome formulas. Although the replication of all segments relies on a common replication-associated protein (Rep), the molecular basis underlying segment-specific differences in genome abundance remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether protein-DNA interactions at conserved cis-regulatory elements are associated with this variability by focusing on the intergenic region (IR) of segment S of milk vetch dwarf virus (MDV). We used a structure-based
papers.summary: This study uses structural modeling to investigate how protein-DNA interactions at conserved regulatory elements may explain why different genome segments of multipartite nanoviruses accumulate at unequal levels during infection. By focusing on the intergenic region of a specific segment of milk vetch dwarf virus, the authors provide a molecular basis for segment-specific differences in genome abundance, which was previously poorly understood.

papers.title: In silico identification of novel PTP1B inhibitors by the investigation of molecular mechanism, QSAR, and DFT studies.
papers.abstract: Protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B (PTP1B) is a well-known and promising drug target involved in the negative regulation of insulin and leptin signaling, and new anti-diabetic molecules for the treatment of type 2 diabetes are directly in its hands. A series of PTP1B inhibitors was discovered and characterized using in silico techniques, including virtual screening, molecular docking, ADMET profiling, toxicity prediction, VEGA-QSAR analysis, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. A starting library of 1000 anti-diabetic compounds was screened, and Pu
papers.summary: This study used computational methods to identify potential new inhibitors of PTP1B, a key drug target for type 2 diabetes. By screening a library of 1000 anti-diabetic compounds, the researchers found promising candidates through virtual screening, molecular docking, and other in silico analyses.

papers.title: Plasticizers and prostate cancer: unraveling the link through network toxicology and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Plasticizers, as widespread environmental endocrine disruptors, are increasingly linked to an elevated risk of prostate cancer (PCa). However, the specific molecular mechanisms by which they drive PCa initiation and progression remain incompletely elucidated. Addressing this knowledge gap is crucial for assessing environmental health risks and identifying potential intervention targets.
papers.summary: This study uses network toxicology and machine learning to investigate how plasticizers (environmental endocrine disruptors) may contribute to prostate cancer. The authors identify key molecular pathways and potential targets linking plasticizer exposure to cancer initiation and progression.

papers.title: Triptolide targets JUN to reverse cisplatin resistance of ovarian cancer: insights from single-cell transcriptome analysis and machine learning validation.
papers.abstract: Platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC) is a major clinical challenge driven by profound intratumoral heterogeneity. Triptolide (TP) exhibits promising anti-tumor potential, yet its precise mechanisms within PROC remain elusive due to the limitations of traditional target-screening strategies.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell transcriptomics and machine learning to show that the drug triptolide reverses cisplatin resistance in ovarian cancer by targeting the JUN gene. The findings provide a new potential therapeutic strategy for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer.

papers.title: Multi-Target Cardioprotective Potential of Ajuga bracteosa Phytochemicals: An Integrated Network Pharmacology and Molecular Docking Approach.
papers.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI), especially its adrenaline-induced myocardial injury, remains a leading cause of global mortality, often resulting in irreversible cardiac damage and heart failure due to stress cardiomyopathy.
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and molecular docking to identify phytochemicals from Ajuga bracteosa that may protect against adrenaline-induced myocardial infarction by targeting multiple cardiac pathways. The findings suggest these natural compounds could serve as multi-target cardioprotective agents, though experimental validation is needed.

papers.title: Transcriptomic analysis-driven identification and transcriptional characterization of Komagataella phaffii promoters from highly transcribed endogenous genes across diverse culture conditions.
papers.abstract: The yeast Komagataella phaffii (formerly Pichia pastoris) is a robust host for recombinant protein production, capable of growing at high cell densities, performing post-translational modifications, and efficiently secreting heterologous proteins. However, gene expression still relies mainly on the methanol-inducible AOX1 promoter (PAOX1) and the constitutive GAPDH promoter (PGAP), highlighting the need for alternative promoters with distinct regulatory properties. This study aimed to identify and characterize promoters from the most highly transcribed endogenous genes across diverse culture c
papers.summary: This study used transcriptomic analysis to identify and characterize new promoters from highly expressed endogenous genes in the yeast Komagataella phaffii, aiming to expand the limited toolkit of promoters available for recombinant protein production. By analyzing gene expression across diverse culture conditions, the authors discovered alternative promoters with distinct regulatory properties, offering more options for fine-tuning gene expression in this industrial host.

papers.title: The Interaction between the Tyrosine Kinase Receptor EphA2 and RNF5: Structural Insights from an In Silico Approach.
papers.abstract: EphA2 is a tyrosine kinase receptor from the Eph (erythropoietin-producing hepatocellular) family that is involved in several processes associated with regular cellular functions, as well as in different pathological conditions including cancer. EphA2 is up-regulated in many types of tumors, and the process of ligand-triggered receptor endocytosis and the subsequent degradation attract a lot of attention as a means of reducing receptor levels and its pro-oncogenic outcomes. In this context, the intracellular Sam (sterile alpha motif) domain of EphA2 (EphA2-Sam) plays an important role, being t
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods to investigate how the tyrosine kinase receptor EphA2 interacts with the E3 ubiquitin ligase RNF5, focusing on the structural details of the EphA2 Sam domain. The findings provide insights into the molecular mechanisms that could regulate EphA2 degradation, which is relevant for developing cancer therapies aimed at reducing pro-oncogenic EphA2 levels.

papers.title: AAV capsid sites breakdown: large protein insertions impact on vector dynamics.
papers.abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors are one of the most used gene delivery systems, and several capsid engineering strategies have been followed to further improve their performance. Current capsid design approaches predominantly rely on small peptide insertions (<100 a.a.). Integrating large proteins poses challenges due to the nature of protein folding and the complexity of capsid assembly.
papers.summary: This paper analyzes how inserting large proteins into the AAV capsid affects vector dynamics, highlighting challenges beyond those seen with small peptide insertions. It provides a breakdown of capsid sites and their impact on protein folding and capsid assembly.

papers.title: Anti-amyloid nanobody-Fc fusion protein drives potent amyloid clearance through microglial recruitment.
papers.abstract: Anti-amyloid beta (Aβ) monoclonal antibodies are effective at lowering amyloid in Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, whether Fc-mediated effector function is absolutely required for efficacy is not completely understood. This is important for optimizing therapeutic efficacy and mitigating side effects such as amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA). Antibodies lacking Fc effector function, like single-domain antibodies (nanobodies), offer a unique tool to dissect these mechanisms, as their small size facilitates blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration and allows Fc-mediated functions to be
papers.summary: This study uses nanobody-Fc fusion proteins to show that Fc-mediated effector function is critical for amyloid clearance in Alzheimer's disease, as nanobodies lacking Fc were ineffective. The fusion proteins recruited microglia to clear amyloid plaques, suggesting a mechanism that could inform safer therapies by reducing side effects like ARIA.
